name: MonarchTabs
title: Tabs
wrapsNative: Button per tab, ViewThatFits, ScrollView with ScrollViewReader, matchedGeometryEffect, AccessibilityTraits.isTabBar and .isSelected
summary: A strip of tabs for the top of a screen or a section, with a line or a pill on the selected tab, optional counts and sideways scrolling. SwiftUI has no such control.
whenToUse: To switch between views of related content in the same place: the sections of a record, filtered lists with counts. The app shows the content for the selection below the strip.
whenNotToUse: For two to four short, equal choices use Picker with pickerStyle(.segmented). For the top-level destinations of an app use TabView (see bottom-tab-bar).
api: MonarchTabs.init(_ label: String, selection: Binding<Value>, items: [MonarchTabsItem<Value>], variant: MonarchTabsVariant = .line)
MonarchTabsItem.init(_ title: String, value: Value, count: String? = nil, countTone: MonarchTone = .neutral, isDisabled: Bool = false)

options.name: label
options.description: The spoken name of the strip, for example "Project sections". It is not shown.

options.name: selection
options.description: The value of the selected tab. Value is any Hashable type.

options.name: items
options.description: The tabs, in order. Each has a title, a unique value, and optionally a count, a count tone and isDisabled.

options.name: variant
options.description: line: a line under the selected tab and a hairline under the strip. pill: a raised pill on a muted track.

states.name: selected
states.description: The label takes the default text colour, with a 2-point accent line under it (line) or a bordered surface pill behind it (pill).

states.name: unselected
states.description: The label uses the muted text colour.

states.name: disabled tab
states.description: The label uses the disabled text colour and the tab cannot be chosen. Set per item with isDisabled, or for the strip with disabled(_:).

states.name: with a count
states.description: A subtle MonarchBadge in the count tone follows the label.

states.name: selection changes
states.description: The line or pill moves to the new tab over the fast duration, or at once with Reduce Motion.

states.name: tabs do not fit
states.description: The strip scrolls sideways, without indicators, and a newly selected tab is scrolled into view.

appearance: Labels use the label type role in the muted text role, the default text role when selected and the disabled text role when disabled. The line variant has a hairline in the default border role under the strip and a 2-point line in the strong accent role under the selected tab. The pill variant has a track in the muted background role and a selected pill in the surface role with a default border. Counts are subtle badges in the tone roles.
platformNotes: The parity map lists Tabs as build on iOS and as a theme on Material's tab row on Android. The web composes Tabs, TabsList, TabsTrigger and TabsContent; here one view takes the items and the selection, and the content is the app's own switch on the selection, as with Picker. Not offered: the web's link tabs (TabsNav, TabsLink), which are tab-styled links between pages (on iOS switching screens is navigation, not tabs), TabsFilter, which is this component with a selection that can be cleared, the accent count tone (MonarchTone has no accent), and arbitrary content in a trigger. The web's arrow-key movement between tabs is the system's Full Keyboard Access here. The web's scrollable flag is not a parameter: labels always stay on one line, and the strip scrolls by itself when the tabs do not fit the width. The pill track is 44 points high instead of the web's 36, so each tab meets the touch target.
accessibility: The strip is a container with the tab bar trait, named by label.
Each tab is a Button with the selected trait when it is the selection, so VoiceOver reads the name, "selected" and the position.
The count is part of the tab's name, after the title: "Open, 12". The visible badge is not read a second time.
The selection is marked by a line or a bordered pill, not by colour alone.
Each tab has a touch target at least 44 points high and wide.
Labels scale with Dynamic Type and stay on one line; when the tabs do not fit, the strip scrolls sideways.
The indicator moves without animation when Reduce Motion is on.
The order of the tabs follows the layout direction.
edgeCases: A selection that matches no item shows no indicator; every tab is unselected.
Values must be unique in the strip; they identify the tabs.
An empty count string shows no badge.
In the pill variant a neutral count has the same muted background as the track, so it shows as plain text. The web uses a darker fill there.
A scrolling strip gives no visible sign that more tabs follow, other than a tab cut off at the edge. Keep the number of tabs small.
A single label wider than the screen is not wrapped; it scrolls. Keep labels to one or two words.
With an empty items array the strip has no height apart from the line or the track padding.

examples.title: Line and pill
examples.setupTemplate:
@State private var lineSel = {{groups.0.selected}}
@State private var pillSel = {{groups.1.selected}}
examples.setup:
@State private var lineSel = "board"
@State private var pillSel = "week"
examples.code:
VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: MonarchTokens.Space.space4) {
    MonarchTabs(
        "Views",
        selection: $lineSel,
        items: [
            MonarchTabsItem("Board", value: "board"),
            MonarchTabsItem("List", value: "list"),
            MonarchTabsItem("Timeline", value: "timeline", isDisabled: true),
        ],
        variant: .line
    )
    Text(["board": "Board view", "list": "List view"][lineSel] ?? "")
        .monarchTextStyle(.body)
    MonarchTabs(
        "Range",
        selection: $pillSel,
        items: [
            MonarchTabsItem("Day", value: "day"),
            MonarchTabsItem("Week", value: "week"),
            MonarchTabsItem("Month", value: "month"),
        ],
        variant: .pill
    )
    Text(["day": "Day", "week": "Week", "month": "Month"][pillSel] ?? "")
        .monarchTextStyle(.body)
}

examples.title: A compact switch between views
examples.code:
MonarchTabs(
    "View",
    selection: $view,
    items: [
        MonarchTabsItem("Board", value: 0),
        MonarchTabsItem("List", value: 1),
        MonarchTabsItem("Timeline", value: 2),
    ],
    variant: .pill
)
